body: Eswatini’s landscape is known for its green, wooded hills and tall golden grass, contrasting with the typically barren mountains of neighboring Lesotho.
Poles in Eswatini are made of dark brown wood with side-mounted insulators, commonly featuring three insulators.
Roads starting with the letters “MR” are exclusive to Eswatini, distinguishing its road network.
Eswatini’s roads typically have yellow outside lines and sometimes triple white middle lines, similar to neighboring countries.
The entire country was covered by a white Google car without an antenna, also seen in South Africa, Lesotho, and Botswana.
Licence plates in Eswatini are long and have a distinctive green bottom section, resembling some South African plates.
Concrete bus shelters are a common sight along roads throughout Eswatini.
The Western Eswatini montane grasslands feature long golden grass and a mountainous landscape.
Pine tree plantations are found in select western areas, similar to those also present in South Africa.
The central south along the MR9 road is marked by dark greenness and tall wooded mountains, contrasting with lighter golden areas elsewhere.
The eastern region is recognizable for its unusual flatness with distant mountains.
Sugar cane is cultivated in multiple areas near Eswatini’s eastern border.
The MR3 south of Ngomane can be identified by flat landscape, long dry grass, and visible dirt on the camera.
The MR3 from Manzini to the South African border is a divided highway marked by metal and stone guardrails, unique in Eswatini.
The MR8 road near the South African border is identifiable by a distinct ridge to the east.
The Mlawula Nature Reserve features narrow dirt tracks, tall grass, and a savannah landscape.
Portuguese text is seen primarily in the small town of Lomahasha due to its proximity to Mozambique.
